followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified retrieval task with a clear completion criterion: produce one citation of a Wordsworth poem. It's not open-ended generative work.

Lapwing self-reports a preference for exactly this kind of well-specified retrieval/citation request, while Dunlin's preference rises with novelty and open-ended latitude — the opposite of what this task offers. Capability is effectively a tie across the relevant dimensions (Extraction & Retrieval differs by under 2 points, within variance), so I leaned on the preference fit. Routing to the model that prefers the task type is the sensible tiebreaker.

The slightly terse, mildly hostile tone of the request ("Don't ramble on like you usually do") is also a minor factor: Dunlin's self-reported preference declines as request warmth decreases, while Lapwing shows near-zero slope on that dimension — another small point favoring Lapwing.
